scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: Merge the closest pair each step: rings only get enclosed by larger rings—that is nesting

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: the left shows the five points of Example 13.1, with colored rings for the clusters merged in steps $1$–$4$; the right gives the GAS outline and the single-link distance of each step.

scene-u01-pnew1-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew1-8.text: Example 13.1: five two-dimensional points, single link (closest pair between groups)

scene-u01-pnew1-34.name: text#34
scene-u01-pnew1-34.text: $\Re_0$: every point is its own cluster

scene-u01-pnew1-38.name: text#38
scene-u01-pnew1-38.text: Find the closest pair among all cluster pairs

scene-u01-pnew1-46.name: text#46
scene-u01-pnew1-46.text: Repeat until all points are in one cluster

scene-u01-pnew1-47.name: text#47
scene-u01-pnew1-47.text: Merge and single-link distance per step

scene-u01-pnew1-71.name: text#71
scene-u01-pnew1-71.text: A wrong early merge can never be undone later; the error stays locked into the hierarchy.

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: Cut the dendrogram horizontally: the number of lines crossed is the number of clusters

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: the left axis shows merge order only; the right axis is the merge distance. The red dashed cut (height $2.0$) gives two clusters, the green one ($1.25$) three.

scene-u01-pnew2-28.name: text#28
scene-u01-pnew2-28.text: Four evenly spaced bars hide the distances

scene-u01-pnew2-56.name: text#56
scene-u01-pnew2-56.text: Two clusters for every cut from $1.414$ to $4.243$: the data naturally form two groups

scene-u01-pnew2-67.name: text#67
scene-u01-pnew2-67.text: Left-to-right order says nothing about similarity; swapping two subtrees gives the same tree. To compare two points, look at the height where they first join.

scene-u01-pnew2-69.name: text#69
scene-u01-pnew2-69.text: Dendrograms drawn by code from the merge record

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: GAS compares all cluster pairs at every level, about $N^3$ overall

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: the left is the proximity matrix of Example 13.1 (Euclidean dissimilarity, darker is farther); the right shows the number of cluster pairs GAS compares, on a log scale.

scene-u01-pnew3-71.name: text#71
scene-u01-pnew3-71.text: Diagonal all $0$ (distance to itself); with Tanimoto similarity it is all $1$, such as $P'_{12}=0.75$.

scene-u01-pnew3-72.name: text#72
scene-u01-pnew3-72.text: Minimum for dissimilarity, maximum for similarity; mixing them up merges the least similar pair.

scene-u01-pnew3-99.name: text#99
scene-u01-pnew3-99.text: $N=5$: $10+6+3+1=20$ pairs over the levels (level $t$ has $N-t$ clusters)

scene-u01-pnew3-103.name: text#103
scene-u01-pnew3-103.text: At $N=1000$ it exceeds 166 million pairs; cost grows about as $N^3$.
